exact_statement: For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign f, let a_S=fhat(S), p_S=a_S^2, ell_S=log2(1/p_S) on positive atoms and a_S ell_S=0 otherwise, c_U=sum_S a_S a_(S xor U) ell_S, E_log=sum_(U nonempty)|U|c_U^2, and J_R=sum_(U nonempty)p_(R xor U)/|U|. Every occupied R obeys p_R[H(f)-ell_R]^2<=J_R E_log; also sum_(U nonempty)c_U^2=Var_p(ell). For a largest atom, H(f)<=ell_R+sqrt(J_R E_log/p_R).

exact_statement: There is no finite universal K with E_log(f)<=K I(f), nor any finite universal K with sqrt(J_R E_log(f)/p_R)<=K I(f) for the largest-atom anchor R of every Boolean f. The first is refuted by n-bit one-point defects with E_log/I~4n^2; the second by disjoint tensor powers of the three-bit point defect, whose anchor cost is exponentially large while influence is linear.
